title: Hello World
description: Your first programming challenge! Write a function that returns 'Hello World'.
instructions: Create a function called `solution()` that returns the string 'Hello World'.
hints: Start by declaring a function using the function keyword
Functions can return values using the 'return' keyword
Strings are text enclosed in quotes
The function should return exactly 'Hello World'
Solution: function solution() { return 'Hello World'; }

title: Add Two Numbers
description: Learn about function parameters and arithmetic operations.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(a, b)` that takes two numbers and returns their sum.
hints: Functions can accept parameters (inputs)
Parameters are listed in parentheses after the function name
Use the + operator to add numbers
Return the result using the return keyword
Solution: return a + b;

title: Is Even?
description: Learn about conditionals and the modulo operator.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(num)` that returns true if the number is even, false otherwise.
hints: The modulo operator (%) gives the remainder of division
Even numbers have a remainder of 0 when divided by 2
Use the === operator to check for equality
You can return the result of a comparison directly
Solution: return num % 2 === 0;

title: Maximum of Two
description: Learn to compare values and use conditional logic.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(a, b)` that returns the larger of two numbers.
hints: Use the > operator to compare values
You can use an if-else statement or a ternary operator
The ternary operator syntax is: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse
If a is greater than b, return a, otherwise return b
Solution: return a > b ? a : b;

title: String Length
description: Learn about string properties and methods.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(str)` that returns the length of a string.
hints: Strings have a built-in length property
Access properties using dot notation
The length property doesn't need parentheses (it's not a method)
Return the length directly
Solution: return str.length;

title: Celsius to Fahrenheit
instructions: Create a function called `solution(celsius)` that converts Celsius to Fahrenheit using the formula: F = C × 9/5 + 32
hints: Use the formula: F = C × 9/5 + 32
Follow the order of operations (multiplication before addition)
You can write 9/5 directly in JavaScript
Return the calculated value
Solution: return celsius * 9/5 + 32;

title: Absolute Value
description: Learn about conditionals and absolute values.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(num)` that returns the absolute value of a number (always positive).
hints: If a number is negative, negate it to make it positive
Use the < operator to check if a number is negative
Negate a number using the - operator
If the number is already positive or zero, return it as is
Solution: return num < 0 ? -num : num;

title: First Character
description: Learn about string indexing and accessing characters.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(str)` that returns the first character of a string.
hints: Strings can be accessed like arrays
Use square brackets [] to access a character by index
Indexing starts at 0 (first character is at index 0)
Return the character at index 0
Solution: return str[0];

title: Is Positive?
description: Practice with comparisons and boolean logic.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(num)` that returns true if the number is positive (greater than 0), false otherwise.
hints: Use the > operator to check if a number is greater than 0
The comparison returns a boolean (true or false)
You can return the comparison result directly
Zero is not considered positive
Solution: return num > 0;

title: Circle Area
description: Calculate the area of a circle using formulas.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(radius)` that calculates the area of a circle using the formula: A = π × r²
hints: Use the formula: A = π × r²
JavaScript provides Math.PI for the value of π
r² means r multiplied by r
Multiply Math.PI by radius * radius
Solution: return Math.PI * radius * radius;
